chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mas'ada ibn Sadqa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever visits a patient, a caller from the sky will call out to him by name: O so-and-so, you have done good, and your walking (visiting) has been made good for you by the rewards from Paradise.'

key_terms.طَابَ لَكَ مَمْشَاكَ: your walking/visiting has been made good/favorable for you
key_terms.طِبْتَ: you have done good / you are pure

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a sick person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the spiritual elevation of visiting the sick, framing it as a direct conduit for divine recognition. The celestial proclamation not only validates the visitor's character but also serves as a tangible promise of Paradise, reinforcing the concept of 'iyadat al-marid as a key act of worship in Shia tradition.
